$comment: Documents every company.json key (plan §3.3 + §20 additions). This file is DOCUMENTATION read by humans and by company.py's error messages; the actual validation logic is hand-written stdlib Python in company.py (no jsonschema dependency) — see validate_company() there. Keys not listed here are unknown and refused by company.py validate.
$registries_comment: A company home is resolved from ~/.claude/knowledge/gtm_company_registry.json FIRST (a GTM-only, machine-local registry — {"schema_version":1,"companies":{"<slug>":{"root":"<path>"}}} — written only via `company.py register`/`unregister`, for a home with no GitHub remote, since scripts/repo_manifest.py's own `register` refuses those), then ~/.claude/knowledge/repo_registry.json for a slug not already in the GTM registry (CSA/Agency keep resolving there). A slug in BOTH registries is INVALID.
slug: string, required. Must match the registry key used to resolve this pack.
business_model: string enum, required: local_service | b2b_saas | ecommerce | other.

accounts.credential_ref: string, required. Shape 'gsm:<name>' | 'browser:<server>' | 'none', where <name> is [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ and <server> is LOWERCASE-ONLY [a-z0-9-]+ (an uppercase server name like 'browser:Playwright-GTM' does NOT match and is INVALID). A credential_ref value (other than 'none') that appears in more than one registered pack is INVALID.
accounts.$comment_extra_keys: accounts[] entries MAY carry additional, system-specific keys beyond the ones above -- the validator accepts them silently (free-form extension, never itself validated). Real examples from the Brightline pack fixture, by system: google_ads: ocid, conversion_id, conversion_labels (list[string]), call_conversion_number; gtm: gtm_account_id, gtm_container_id; ga4: ga4_account_id, ga4_property_id; gbp: store_code; facebook: asset_id. These are read by downstream tooling (e.g. host_systems path-scoping, ad-platform conversion wiring) that knows to look for them on a given system's account entry -- they are documentation-by-example here, not an enumerated/closed key list.

ai_content_policy.mode: string enum: disclose_never_strip | strip_before_publish | forbid, required.

autonomy.level: string enum, required: shadow | autonomous (per §20.6, superseding the earlier advisory|shadow|semi|autonomous ladder).

standing_approvals.rows: list[string tier_table.json row id], required. A bare '*' wildcard anywhere in this list is INVALID.

operator_input: string, required. 'from_manifest' means authoritative = the home's manifest.json operator_input.

paths.metrics: string, required (home-relative file path). NEVER ignored by `company.py gitignore` — §3.2 tracks metrics.json/METRICS.md.
paths.feature_inventory_dir: string, required (home-relative). NEVER ignored, even when nested under activity_log_dir.
paths.build_dir: string, optional (home-relative). When set, build_dir/** is ignored by `company.py gitignore` (build output, e.g. Brightline's tracking/build/).
paths._relative_path_rule: EVERY paths.* value (except mission_records, which is an enum not a path) must be relative to the company home: no leading '/' or '~', and no '..' path component anywhere. An absolute or escaping path is INVALID.

class_o_batches: list[string], optional (§6.4 R9 Class O batch ids).
mirror_dir: string, optional (home-relative or absolute path for owner-facing mirrors).
mirror_basename: string, optional. Base filename (no extension) for the owner-facing mirror files written into mirror_dir — <mirror_basename>.md and <mirror_basename>.html. Default: '<legal_name-or-slug title-cased with spaces>_Activity_Log' (e.g. Brightline's is literally 'Brightline_Activity_Log', matching the pre-migration file the operator already uses at ~/Desktop/Brightline/Brightline_Activity_Log.html). Only meaningful when mirror_dir is set.
mirror_title: string, optional. The mirror's page/header title (e.g. 'Brightline Activity Log', matching display_names[0] + ' Activity Log' for the Brightline migration exactly). Default: display_names[0] (falling back to legal_name, never the lowercase slug) + ' Activity Log'. Only meaningful when mirror_dir is set.
regulated: list[string], optional. Only value ever valid today: 'hipaa' (§20.5). Any other value is INVALID.
host_systems: object, optional: {host_glob: system}. 'host_glob' is a plain host/domain string (suffix-matched exactly like harvest_tool_trail.py's DEFAULT_HOST_SYSTEMS — 'glob' here describes the matching behavior, never fnmatch syntax), checked BEFORE the runtime defaults so a pack can override or extend the default host->system mapping for its own domains (e.g. {"business.google.com": "gbp_remodeling", "facebook.com": "facebook_remodeling", "example-remodeling.com": "website_remodeling"}). Every value must be a member of this pack's own system set (scope.channels_in_scope union the runtime's fixed extras — the same union activity_log.py's SYSTEMS computes) — an unregistered system name is INVALID. #27 CAVEAT: host_systems is HOST-LEVEL ONLY by default — a plain host key cannot tell two brands apart when they share a host (e.g. two sibling brands of the same company both using business.google.com and facebook.com). For that, a key MAY instead be `<host>/<path-prefix>` (e.g. "business.google.com/9000000000000000001", a GBP location id, or "facebook.com/100000000000001", a Facebook Page id) — despite the name 'path-prefix', this is NOT a prefix match: the id is matched when it appears at a token boundary (not immediately preceded or followed by another alphanumeric character) ANYWHERE in the URL's path or query string, checked BEFORE any plain host-only entry for the same host, so the more specific mapping always wins. A plain host-only entry, if also present, is the fallback when no path-prefix entry's id appears in the URL. If more than one path-prefix entry's id matches the same URL (e.g. both brands' ids appear in it), the FIRST matching entry in this object's own key insertion order wins.

co_managing_systems.interface: string, required (e.g. 'api' | 'web_ui' — which surface the co-managing identity uses, per §20.13's identity+interface keying for change-history attribution).
co_managing_systems.mode: string enum, required: read_only (the only value ever valid today — a co-managing identity is never a writer per §20.9's Model A decision).

legacy_workdirs: list of strings, optional. Absolute (or ~/) paths of directories where this company's GTM sessions ran BEFORE its home was registered (no '..'). harvest_tool_trail adds their Claude Code project dirs to its default transcript search so pre-migration sessions are still attributed. Private to the pack; the runtime code never hardcodes a company path.
shared_identifiers_note: See shared_identifiers above — repeated here because §20.9 also cites it for the Agency co-managing relationship.
